entry.summary: The Valhalla Spider is Aston Martin's first mid-engined open-cockpit supercar and the fastest Aston Martin ever built without a fixed roof, reaching 217 mph with the cockpit open or the optional carbon fiber hardtop in place. A twin-turbo V8 and three electric motors make a combi
entry.content:
The Valhalla Spider is Aston Martin's first mid-engined open-cockpit supercar and the fastest Aston Martin ever built without a fixed roof, reaching 217 mph with the cockpit open or the optional carbon fiber hardtop in place. A twin-turbo V8 and three electric motors make a combined 1,064 horsepower, with two of the motors driving the front wheels. In Race mode, an active rear wing rises 10 inches and also works as an airbrake when you brake hard. With the roof off, a wind deflector clips in, and when the roof goes back on, the deflector folds into three pieces that stow in compartments in the door sills. The carbon fiber doors swing upward, and a new touring seat makes it easier to climb in with the roof on, though the Valhalla coupe's carbon race seat is a no-cost option. Deliveries begin in the third quarter of 2027.

entry.content:
In 1973, Honda named its first two-stroke motocross bike the Elsinore after the motorcycle race at Lake Elsinore, California, which Steve McQueen once entered under a made-up name. This 1979 CR125R Elsinore reportedly remained in the steel and wood crate it was originally delivered in. Plastic still wraps the exhaust and swingarm, smaller parts are packed separately beside the frame, and the American Honda cardboard box that covered the crate, stamped Made in Japan, is part of the sale. Under the packing is a red 123cc two-stroke motocrosser with a six-speed gearbox and a tall 23-inch front wheel. It has no title, is offered for off-road use only, and is now up for auction.

entry.content:
The Submariner Roll Neck takes its cues from the practical knitwear once issued to the Royal Navy, but replaces traditional naval wool with five-gauge cashmere. The heavier knit gives the sweater a substantial feel, while a jersey stitch keeps the surface clean and familiar. Drop shoulders reinforce its relaxed, utilitarian character, and the 1x1 rib roll neck provides a warm finish suited to colder weather. Handmade in Scotland from 100% cashmere, it preserves the straightforward spirit of a naval classic while turning an inherently rugged garment into something considerably more luxurious.

entry.content:
Two decades of maturation and a historic partnership with Spanish sherry producer Valdespino distinguish The Macallan TIME : SPACE Sherry Cask. The 20-year-old single malt begins its journey in sherry-seasoned oak casks before undergoing a second marrying period in casks seasoned with The Macallan's own Valdespino sherry. Selected from the first 200 casks prepared at the Valdespino bodega in Jerez de la Frontera, they arrived in Scotland during The Macallan's bicentennial celebrations in 2024. This dual-stage approach marks a new chapter in the distillery's longstanding relationship with Spanish oak and sherry craftsmanship.

entry.content:
A24's movie cat encyclopedia has more than 1,000 entries, from famous names like Puss in Boots and Austin Powers' Mr. Bigglesworth to unnamed alley cats on screen for only a few seconds. Entries run alphabetically and cover the range of roles cats have played on screen: household pets, villains, spaceship crew, cat-woman hybrids, including Holly Golightly's orange tabby from Breakfast at Tiffany's and Jones from the Alien franchise. Original essays cover recurring cat archetypes like Bad Omen Cats and Talking Cats, alongside profiles of real cat actors with their own IMDb credits. The book runs 420 pages in a buckram-wrapped hardcover, with more than 1,900 film stills throughout.

Toyota's Land Cruiser started in 1951 as the Jeep BJ and became the Land Cruiser in 1954, once Toyota had to drop the Jeep name, which belonged to Willys-Overland. The 75th Anniversary Special Edition, built on the Land Cruiser 250, is sold through Toyota Germany and limited to 75 vehicles. It is fitted with round headlights with a retro look, 18-inch wheels, and badges at the back and in the cabin, and Smoky Blue, a paint reserved for this edition, is optional. Each buyer also receives a gift box with an enamel sign, a 1:60-scale Tomica model car, a handmade leather key fob, and an updated edition of Alexander Wohlfarth's book Legend Land Cruiser.

entry.summary: Lüm-Tec has built watches for the U.S. government and SWAT teams, and its own Combat B line was tested in desert heat and on frozen mountaintops. The Combat B72's 43mm stainless steel case is forged for strength, bead-blasted against scratches and coated in gunmetal. Its dial car
entry.content:
Lüm-Tec has built watches for the U.S. government and SWAT teams, and its own Combat B line was tested in desert heat and on frozen mountaintops. The Combat B72's 43mm stainless steel case is forged for strength, bead-blasted against scratches and coated in gunmetal. Its dial carries more than 30 layers of Super-Luminova, a glow-in-the-dark material, over a reflective base. A domed sapphire crystal cuts glare, and the watch is water resistant to 656 feet, with double seals at the crown and threaded caseback. Its strap lugs curve downward to wrap the wrist, so it wears smaller than it measures. Two nylon straps, in black and gray, are looped through both sides, so the watch stays on the wrist even if a spring bar, the pin holding a strap end, is damaged. Lüm-Tec replaces the battery and pressure-tests it free for life, and only 500 numbered pieces will be made worldwide.
